Users of the latest version of Claude Code on macOS and Linux can now send messages between different sessions to share findings, ask questions, and coordinate work. Details below.

Claude Code gets cross-session messaging

Anthropic announced a new feature earlier today that should be popular with users who frequently run multiple Claude Code sessions simultaneously.

Starting from Claude Code v2.1.224, different sessions can send messages to each other to share updates and other relevant information; this is particularly useful when users have multiple sessions working on different parts of the same project at the same time.

Here's Anthropic's documentation for this new feature:

Anthropic says the best use cases for this new feature include: handing off research findings, coordinating parallel worktrees, getting status on long-running tasks, and replying to messages across machines.

The company added that users don't need to write the message content themselves. Users just need to type what they want to convey in the prompt, and Claude will automatically write the actual message.

It's worth noting that the cross-session messaging feature does not apply to approving permission requests or changing settings. Commands such as /compact will appear as plain text rather than being executed as actual commands; if processing a message requires permissions, the receiving session will still prompt the user for approval.

To learn more about Claude Code's new cross-session messaging feature, visit this link.
